For the 29 hours between then and now, fifteen devices carrying twenty-two probes were skipped by the heartbeat.

THE MECHANISM, and it is ordinary Python: discovery.load_module execs each probe file off its path, so the probe binds the CURRENT cairn.tools.base.probe.Probe, while the daemon's own frame still held cairn.base.probe.Probe from before the move. The two remaining faces are the same staleness from the other side: constrain and orient failed with ImportError for common_shape_record and AmbiguousComponent, both symbols added to cairn.tools.chain.grammar AFTER the process started. One root cause, two error classes, and neither of them names the loop.

THE BENCH MADE IT SELF-SEALING. A benched device is passed to discover() in skip, so it is never re-scanned, its trouble stops recurring, and its count freezes. Four tickets sat at ~10,286 occurrences with last_seen 23.7 hours old — which reads as an outage that ended. It had not ended; it had gone total. An outage that stops recurring is indistinguishable from one that was fixed.

A RESTART ALONE WOULD NOT HAVE FIXED IT, which is the trap for whoever meets this next. loop.py:50 defines the bench as 'a live ticket by this name exists', and clearing is the recipient's act alone — so a restarted loop keeps every device dark, silently, with the imports now perfectly fine and nothing red anywhere. The order is restart, verify through the loop's own discover(), then clear.

The predicate that was missing is one comparison and every input to it is already free on disk: is this process older than the code it is judging. Process start time, file mtimes, and the module file behind a class object are all readable, and the check only ever runs on the failure path — so a healthy system pays nothing for it.

It is not — BreadcrumbLog(device, instance) is a plain constructor and any module can build one and hand it a record TODAY, with no new code. A walk is one crossing with a path, not three crossings. This keeps an ordinary cheapest-first resolution from reading as three failures while still answering 'why was it slow'.

A CACHE HIT IS A BOUNDARY NOT CROSSED, and saying so is what turns this trail from present into useful. The domain already keeps a meter (yield_report: tokens SPENT on misses against tokens AVOIDED by hits), so the trail will describe the same events a store already describes — a Law 7 exposure rather than a redundancy. The falsifier and the watch are both built on that: they ask the two records to AGREE over a window, which is also the only clause of this proof whose evidence the proof cannot write both halves of, since the store side is written by resolve()'s existing path.

A DISTINCTION THE FLOOR'S CHARTER DOES NOT YET DRAW, owed as a charter delta by this build. diagnostic.py's discipline paragraph says instrumentation is 'targeted and TEMPORARY... not standing probes left hanging', which was written when home was an in-memory mailbox and the risk was flooding a live process.
